matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: Compute the integer values of both sides, find the numeric difference, and look for a single‑stick move that changes a numeral or operator by exactly that amount, thereby balancing the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is false and the numeric imbalance can be corrected by a single‑stick change.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick that changes a numeral by an amount that does not match the required difference, leaving the equation still unbalanced.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and a V appears, relocate one of V’s diagonal sticks so that it becomes an X, increasing the value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by 5 and a V is present.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal stick from a V and leaving a single diagonal line, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Swap I and V in IV to make VI (adds 2)
matchstick.principle: When the imbalance is exactly 2 and the pattern IV appears, move the vertical stick of the I onto the V to turn IV into VI, adding 2.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by 2 and the left side contains the numeral IV.
matchstick.example: Swapping sticks between I and V but ending up with an invalid numeral order or value.

matchstick.title: Change + to - and add I
matchstick.principle: If a plus sign is present and the equation can be fixed by decreasing the right‑hand side, move the vertical stick from the plus to form a minus sign and add an I stick elsewhere to adjust the value.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is too large on the right side and a plus sign is present.
matchstick.example: Changing a plus sign to a minus sign without adding an extra I, resulting in the wrong numeric adjustment.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: When the equation is off by 1 and there are isolated I’s, relocate a vertical stick from one I to another numeral to increase or decrease its value by 1.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance is 1 and at least one I is present.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from one I to another, but creating an invalid numeral (e.g., a lone diagonal stick).

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign; never move its sticks
matchstick.principle: Never relocate any matchsticks that belong to the '=' sign; altering it would break the equality operator and invalidate the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: In every matchstick puzzle; the equality sign must remain unchanged.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from the '=' sign, breaking the equality operator.

matchstick.title: Change - to = by adding a horizontal stick from a numeral
matchstick.principle: If a minus sign appears and the numeric imbalance is large, move a horizontal stick from a numeral (e.g., from an I) onto the minus sign to turn it into an '=' sign, adjusting the equation accordingly.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is far off and converting the subtraction into equality can balance it.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal stick from a numeral to add to the minus sign, turning it into '=', but leaving the source numeral invalid.

matchstick.title: Relocate minus sign to a different position
matchstick.principle: When a minus sign is present, consider moving its single horizontal stick to a new location in the equation, possibly to the other side of the '=', to create a valid subtraction that balances the numbers.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is false and moving the minus sign could adjust the arithmetic to become true.
matchstick.example: Moving the minus sign to a location that leaves no operator on one side, resulting in an incomplete equation.

matchstick.title: When converting - to +, also move a vertical stick to form a valid plus sign
matchstick.principle: If you need to change a minus sign into a plus sign, you must also relocate a vertical stick from somewhere else to the minus sign location, forming a complete '+' operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When turning a subtraction into addition could fix the equation.
matchstick.example: Changing a minus sign to a plus sign without adding the required vertical stick, leaving an incomplete plus sign.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from the equality sign
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats all sticks as interchangeable and forgets the rule that the equality sign must stay intact.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never select any stick that is part of the '=' sign for relocation.

matchstick.description: Providing an incomplete equation after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves a stick away from a symbol without ensuring the remaining symbols still form valid Roman numerals or operators.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After moving a stick, verify that every symbol in the equation is still a complete, valid numeral or operator.

matchstick.description: Changing – to + without adding the required vertical stick (resulting in an incomplete plus sign)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the horizontal part and overlooks that a plus sign needs both a horizontal and a vertical stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When converting '-' to '+', also move a vertical stick to the same location to complete the plus sign.

matchstick.description: Using an angled stick as a vertical stick (or vice versa), creating an invalid numeral or operator
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any stick can be placed anywhere, ignoring orientation constraints between diagonal and vertical sticks.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Only move sticks to positions that match their orientation; verify that the resulting symbols are valid according to Roman numeral stick shapes.
